A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of early childhood educators of the deaf are not providing the cultural and linguistic role model opportunities for deaf children that are necessary for optimal development.
the use of role models and cultural and linguistic activities in early childhood settings is not widespread.

EC settings need to provide deaf children with more opportunities to interact with fluent linguistic and cultural role models, and teachers should be trained to use research based strategies and materials that are consistent with the cultural perspective.
The main takeaway from our work is that

EC settings should incorporate a cultural perspective of deafness and should be aware of the critical importance of providing deaf children with fluent cultural and linguistic role model experiences in their early years.
EC settings can do a better job in providing deaf children with opportunities to learn from fluent linguistic and cultural role models.
the deaf community and the field of deaf education need to work together to develop a shared understanding of what is best for deaf children and how to achieve it.
